You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE museum (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Num_of_Staff INT,
    Open_Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visitor (
    ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Level_of_membership INT,
    Age INT,
    UNIQUE (ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visit (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    visitor_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Num_of_Ticket INT,
    Total_spent REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (visitor_ID) REFERENCES visitor(ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Museum_ID) REFERENCES museum(Museum_ID)
);

To get “details about rich visitors,” you need to define what “rich” means in your data. In this schema, the best proxy is usually **Total_spent** in the `visit` table (optionally aggregated per visitor).

Here are common options:

### 1) Visitors who spent a lot on a single visit
```sql
SELECT v.ID, v.Name, v.Age, v.Level_of_membership,
       vi.Museum_ID, vi.Num_of_Ticket, vi.Total_spent
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
WHERE vi.Total_spent >= 1000
ORDER BY vi.Total_spent DESC;
```
(Change `1000` to your threshold.)

### 2) “Rich” = highest total spending across all visits (top 10)
```sql
SELECT v.ID, v.Name, v.Age, v.Level_of_membership,
       SUM(vi.Total_spent) AS total_spent_all_visits,
       SUM(vi.Num_of_Ticket) AS total_tickets
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Age, v.Level_of_membership
ORDER BY total_spent_all_visits DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

### 3) Visitors who spent above the average total spending (across all visitors)
```sql
WITH per_visitor AS (
  SELECT vi.visitor_ID, SUM(vi.Total_spent) AS total_spent
  FROM visit vi
  GROUP BY vi.visitor_ID
)
SELECT v.ID, v.Name, v.Age, v.Level_of_membership, p.total_spent
FROM per_visitor p
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = p.visitor_ID
WHERE p.total_spent > (SELECT AVG(total_spent) FROM per_visitor)
ORDER BY p.total_spent DESC;
```

Which definition do you want: **(a)** spending per visit, **(b)** total spending across visits, or **(c)** top N / above average? Also, what threshold or “top N” should I use?
You should look at the visitor who bought the most tickets.

```sql
SELECT v.ID,
       v.Name,
       v.Age,
       v.Level_of_membership,
       SUM(vi.Num_of_Ticket) AS total_tickets_bought
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Age, v.Level_of_membership
ORDER BY total_tickets_bought DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
also need to make sure the tickets were bought in one transaction

```sql
SELECT v.ID,
       v.Name,
       v.Age,
       v.Level_of_membership,
       vi.Museum_ID,
       vi.Num_of_Ticket AS tickets_in_one_transaction,
       vi.Total_spent
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY vi.Num_of_Ticket DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
Don't forget to get the visitor's name in the details.

```sql
SELECT v.ID,
       v.Name AS visitor_name,
       v.Age,
       v.Level_of_membership,
       vi.Museum_ID,
       vi.Num_of_Ticket AS tickets_in_one_transaction,
       vi.Total_spent
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY vi.Num_of_Ticket DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
I also need the visitor's age along with the name.

```sql
SELECT v.Name AS visitor_name,
       v.Age  AS visitor_age,
       vi.Museum_ID,
       vi.Num_of_Ticket AS tickets_in_one_transaction,
       vi.Total_spent
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY vi.Num_of_Ticket DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
